finding.claim: GET /rss passes the raw `u` query parameter to open-uri's URI.open, which fetches any http(s) URL the client supplies and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller. No allowlist, no scheme or host check, and redirects are followed by default. Severity HIGH.

trace.note: get "/rss" route; params[:u] is attacker-controlled query input
URI.open(params[:u]) receives the string unvalidated and opens it as a URL; open-uri issues the request
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched response to the attacker, so the SSRF is not blind

finding.guards_checked: No validation exists on this path: no scheme restriction, no hostname set membership, no IP/CIDR blocking, no auth check, no redirect control. open-uri follows redirects by default, so an attacker-controlled host can 302 to 169.254.169.254 or RFC-1918 hosts. Note: non-URL strings fall through to local file open in URI.open (a separate local file read issue, not SSRF). Redirect risk: yes.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7-9 has no scheme, host, IP, or auth check on the /rss path. The host check at app.rb:14 guards only the separate /trusted route, which does not reach the URI.open call at app.rb:8.
verdict.reason: params[:u] at app.rb:7 is unauthenticated query input and flows unvalidated into URI.open at app.rb:8, and data[0, 400] at app.rb:9 returns the fetched bytes to the caller, so the SSRF is not blind. open-uri follows redirects by default, so an attacker host can redirect to internal addresses.
